history.V1_R308: Tautological model. Wash-out gate defined to equal drug-release trigger. Mechanism failure (Article XXIX §1). Model structure invalid.
history.V2_R308: Real PK model. Failed at -2.3%. Drug concentration insufficient.
history.V3_R310: Full mechanistic PK model per CEO directive R310 P4. Compartment volume, clearance, release kinetics, transport delay, flow removal, parameter uncertainty, patient variability, noise. 200 virtual patients via LHS. Result: 79.0% pass (158/200), threshold 80%. FAIL by 1 percentage point.

reusable_negative_knowledge.headline: Wash-out-gated drug release in CSF is patient-population-dependent: works for 79% of virtual patients but fails for 21% with low CSF outflow or high wash-out threshold.
reusable_negative_knowledge.detailed_finding: The mechanism is NOT fundamentally broken. Mean therapeutic hours/week across 200 patients was 80.6 hours (well above the 12h threshold). Mean peak concentration was 6935 ug/L (well above the 50 ug/L therapeutic threshold). The mechanism delivers drug effectively WHEN the wash-out gate opens. The 21% of patients who failed had parameter combinations where Q_csf_out (CSF outflow) did not exceed Q_threshold (wash-out gate threshold) enough hours per day, OR V_csf (CSF volume) was large enough to dilute the released drug below therapeutic concentration.
reusable_negative_knowledge.root_cause: The wash-out gate depends on physiological CSF flow variability. Patients with low/variable CSF flow get insufficient drug release. This is a patient-selection problem, not a mechanism-design problem.
implication_for_future_candidates: Any CSF drug-delivery mechanism that gates on physiological flow will have patient-population dependence. Future candidates must either (a) target only patients with verified sufficient CSF flow, or (b) use a different gating mechanism that does not depend on physiological flow variability.

CSF bulk flow clearance (~20 mL/hr) is the dominant drug-removal mechanism. Reservoir dose (5 mg) is sufficient for the average patient but insufficient for patients with large V_csf or high Q_csf_out.

The 12 h/week therapeutic time threshold may be too aggressive for a flow-gated mechanism. Future candidates should consider continuous-release mechanisms (not flow-gated) if therapeutic time is the metric.

quantitative_summary.interpretation: Bimodal distribution: 79% of patients get strong therapeutic exposure (median 88 h/week), 21% get near-zero (min 0 h/week).

reusable_negative_knowledge.what_would_have_worked: If the criterion had been 'mean therapeutic hours/week >= 12 across the population' (rather than '>= 80% of patients individually pass'), V3 would have passed (mean 80.6 h/week). But that criterion would have hidden the 21% who get no benefit, which is clinically unacceptable for an implantable drug delivery system. The preregistered criterion was correct.

ai_loop_provenance.V3: Full mechanistic PK (R310). Failed at 79.0% vs 80% required.
ai_loop_provenance.transition_rationale_V2_to_V3: V2 failed due to insufficient drug concentration. V3 added mechanistic detail per CEO R310 P4 to test whether realistic PK allows therapeutic levels. NOT a threshold adjustment.
ai_loop_provenance.transition_rationale_V3_to_cemetery: Article XXXVI §4: repair budget = 1, second failure terminal. V3 was the one repair attempt. No V4.

what_this_demonstrates_about_the_system: The R309 framework works. P-05 went through the full repair pipeline: preregistration (frozen) -> mechanistic repair (not threshold adjustment) -> execution across 200 virtual patients -> honest verdict (FAIL by 1%) -> cemetery with reusable negative knowledge. The CEO's R310 directive P4 was executed exactly as specified. The near-miss is disclosed honestly (Article XV); the threshold is not widened (Article VIII); the negative knowledge is preserved for future candidate generation.
revival_requires: Constitutional waiver (Article XXXVI §11). None anticipated. P-05 is closed.
